dish_name: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Bowls
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment.
Cut the sweet potatoes into 1-inch pieces (peeling is up to you). Cut half the red onion into 1-inch pieces. Save the other half for another meal.
Drain and rinse the black beans, then pat them dry with a clean towel.
In a large bowl, toss the sweet potatoes, onion and beans with the olive oil, cinnamon, paprika, cumin, onion powder, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Spread everything on the baking sheet in a single layer. Roast for 30 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the sweet potatoes are tender and browned at the edges.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in a small pot following the package directions for 1 cup.
Divide the rice among 4 containers or bowls, then top with the roasted sweet potatoes and beans.
Spoon 1/4 cup of salsa over each bowl and squeeze lime over the top. For lunches, leave the salsa and lime for when you eat.
To store, cool the bowls and cover them. They keep in the fridge for up to 4 days. Reheat in the microwave for 1 to 2 minutes, then add the salsa and lime.
method_notes: Only one rated version of the bowls could be read: It's a Veg World After All (4.88 from 8 ratings, so the fallback applies). It roasts the sweet potato, red onion and beans together with warm spices over brown rice and says the parts keep for a week. A version from Delicious Meets Healthy had no ratings and adds a yogurt crema and arugula, which this one leaves out to stay vegan. Quick-cooking brown rice is used so the rice finishes while the pan roasts.
